title: SDK integration walkthrough - Argus Retail
topics: Security: SOC2 / KMS / SSO / audit logs
summary: AE and SE walked Argus Retail through Redwood SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, covered auth (API key & SSO patterns), environment setup, and recommended steps for a pilot. SE demoed Console and Optimize features for batching and quantization suggestions. Customer security lead asked about KMS, audit logs, and VPC/private deployments. Redwood agreed to share SOC2 and security pack and schedule a technical deep dive for benchmarking.
next_steps: Alex Chen - Send security pack (SOC2, KMS integration doc) by 2026-10-11
Priya Kapoor - Share sample Python and TypeScript quickstart repo and recording by 2026-10-09
Jordan Lee - Confirm pilot dataset and desired latency targets by 2026-10-13
Schedule 60-min performance deep dive with customer infra team (proposed 2026-10-15)
action_items: Alex Chen - Send pricing and Dedicated capacity options by 2026-10-14
Priya Kapoor - Provide benchmark template and sample curl/python snippets by 2026-10-09
Samir Rao - Provide list of compliance questions and KMS requirements by 2026-10-12
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, account exec for Redwood, and with me is Priya and Diego from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jordan Lee: Good, thanks. Excited to see the SDK stuff - we're planning a small pilot.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Hey all, quick intro - I'm Maya, product. We're trying to add assisted search and recommendations, priority is latency under 200ms for headless search.
[00:20] Priya Kapoor: Awesome. Today we'll do a short Console tour, then do Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns, and finish with Optimize recommendations around batching and quantization.
[00:32] Samir Rao: I might jump in on security questions later, mostly KMS/SOC2/SSO stuff.
[00:36] Alex Chen: Great. Quick qualification - what's your stack? Jordan?
[00:40] Jordan Lee: We're on Node for front-end services, Python for backend microservices. Infra is AWS, we use VPC endpoints for DBs. Compliance is SOC2 in process, we use HashiCorp Vault for keys.
[00:51] Priya Kapoor: Perfect, that's a common setup. For SDKs we support official Python and TypeScript packages, and both work with REDWOOD_API_KEY env var or SSO/SAML flows in Private deployments.
[00:59] Diego Morales: I'll share my screen to show the SDK quickstart. You should see the Console first - per-route latency and token-level cost.
[01:06] [screen share starts; slight background noise]
[01:12] Diego Morales: Console -> Projects -> Argus-demo. Here you can pin models, set rollout rules, and see Optimize suggestions. For example, Optimize suggests a quantization profile and batch size 8 for short-sequence prompts to drop token cost ~40% while keeping latency under 200ms on our MPT-like models.
[01:28] Maya Patel: MPT-like? We have a procurement constraint around open models - are there validated perf numbers?
[01:34] Priya Kapoor: We publish performance profiles in the model catalog; I'll send the link. Note sometimes the transcript mislabels names - "M P T" shows as MPT but it's a specific variant.
[01:46] Jordan Lee: Cool. Show the SDK quickstarts.
[01:49] Diego Morales: Switching to code. First Python: pip install redwood-inference, then set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. Example snippet -
[01:58] Diego Morales: (typing)
[02:00] Diego Morales: from redwood import RedwoodClient
[02:03] Diego Morales: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
[02:07] Diego Morales: resp = client.generate(model="rwd-llm-2", prompt="Summarize product reviews")
[02:12] Jordan Lee: That looks straightforward. What's the auth scheme? Long-lived key? Short-lived via IAM?
[02:18] Priya Kapoor: For hosted API, API keys are standard, rotateable, and you can scope them. For Private or Dedicated, you can integrate your IdP for SSO and exchange short-lived credentials. We also support signed tokens via customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private.
[02:35] Samir Rao: Can you expand on KMS integration? We cannot export plaintext keys from vaults.
[02:41] Priya Kapoor: Sure - with Private deployments we support bringing your own KMS; Redwood can call your KMS for envelope decryption. For hosted we integrate with major KMS providers but keys are stored encrypted. We'll send the KMS integration doc.
[02:54] Maya Patel: On the TS side?
[02:56] Diego Morales: npm i @redwood/inference, then:
[03:00] Diego Morales: import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
[03:03] Diego Morales: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
[03:07] Diego Morales: await client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-chat-1', messages: [...] })
[03:11] Jordan Lee: How about streaming and function calls? We need tool-calling for retrieval.
[03:16] Priya Kapoor: Streaming is supported in both SDKs and the HTTP API. Function/tool calling is available - the Console shows per-call traces.
[03:23] Alex Chen: On cost: Optimize can recommend batching and cache prefixes. For search use-cases we often enable prefix KV caching to reduce repeated token costs.
[03:31] Jordan Lee: You said KV caching - do you mean KV cache? Some docs say KV cache for decoder states.
[03:35] Priya Kapoor: Yes, KV cache - sorry, sometimes the auto-transcript changes that to K V cash - it's a transcription quirk.
[03:41] Maya Patel: For privacy, we must ensure no PII leaves our environment. If we do a private deployment, is data stored in customer region?
[03:48] Priya Kapoor: With Private deployment, you control the VPC and region. Hosted customers can opt in to data retention policies; we also support per-customer encryption and audit logs.
[03:57] Samir Rao: Audit logs detail per-request metadata? We need them for audits.
[04:01] Diego Morales: Yes, Console includes request-level logs (id, model, tokens, latency) and you can export logs to S3 or a SIEM.
[04:08] Jordan Lee: Great. Performance: we need <200ms P95 for short queries. How do you validate?
[04:14] Priya Kapoor: We run benchmarks using a sample of your workloads. For predictable throughput we recommend Dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs and autoscale rules. The tradeoff is cost vs latency - Dedicated gives lower variance.
[04:26] Maya Patel: Any recommendations for cost optimization?
[04:29] Diego Morales: Use model variants for cheaper tails, quantization, and batching. Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per model and show the expected token cost delta. For e.g. short search prompts, a medium quantized variant with prefix caching often is the best bang-for-buck.
[04:43] Jordan Lee: Quick question on SDK: how to run locally vs in CI?
[04:47] Priya Kapoor: Locally you use REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or a local credentials file. In CI, we recommend injecting short-lived credentials via your secrets manager and never hardcoding keys. For Private deployments you can use service accounts bound to the VPC.
[04:59] Samir Rao: And SSO for console access?
[05:01] Alex Chen: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC at the project/route level. We'll share the SSO guide.
[05:09] Maya Patel: Could you show a live sample of a TypeScript streaming call?
[05:11] Diego Morales: Sure. (types) We create a client, call chat.stream and pipe the chunks to stdout. Streaming demo shows partial tokens and event-based flush. You can also do websocket or SSE.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: Any caveats with Node 18 vs 20?
[05:28] Diego Morales: We recommend Node 18+; some features like native fetch perform better in 20.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: For starting the pilot, what's minimal scope?
[05:36] Alex Chen: A small set of prompts (1000/day) for 2 weeks for accuracy and latency baseline. We can run a benchmarking session against your infra. If results look good, you can opt into Dedicated for production.
[05:47] Maya Patel: Ok sounds good. Samir, any final security blockers?
[05:50] Samir Rao: I'd like the SOC2 report and details on key management and mutual TLS. Also question on data residency - we need EU region for EU customers.
[05:58] Priya Kapoor: We'll include SOC2, KMS integration doc, and details on VPC/private deployment options. For hosted, region selection is supported in EU and NA.
[06:06] Alex Chen: Let's recap next steps - we'll send sample code, security pack, and schedule performance deep dive.
[06:12] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks everyone, recording would be great.
[06:15] Diego Morales: We'll share the recording and the quickstart repo.
[06:18] Alex Chen: Any other questions?
[06:20] Maya Patel: No, that's it. Thanks.
[06:22] Alex Chen: Alright, we'll follow up. Bye.
[06:25] [call ends]
